children: Prabhudas Lilladher's research report on Cummins India

We have revised our EPS estimates downward by -15.0%/-3.9%/-3.7% for FY27E/FY28E/FY29E, respectively, factoring in near-term margin pressures from elevated commodity and freight costs, supply-chain disruptions and an adverse product mix. While the pricing actions implemented in Q2FY27 are expected to provide a gradual offset, we have adopted a relatively cautious outlook on margin recovery, particularly for FY27E. Cummins India (KKC) reported a modest quarterly performance, with revenue growing ~4% YoY to INR32.5bn, supported by moderate growth in domestic sales (+5% YoY to ~INR27bn) and exports (+2% YoY to INR5.7bn). EBITDA margin contracted sharply by 658bps YoY to 18%, primarily due to elevated commodity and freight costs, supply-chain disruptions and an adverse product mix. Despite nearterm margin pressures, demand remain healthy across key domestic markets, including data centres, manufacturing and real estate, alongside continued growth in the distribution business. Exports also recorded sequential improvement (~7% QoQ), indicating resilient underlying demand across end markets. The price hike implemented in Q2FY27 is expected to be progressively realized, supporting a gradual margin recovery over the coming quarters. Looking ahead, demand across domestic and export markets is expected to remain steady, although geopolitical uncertainty, inflationary pressures, commodity price volatility and evolving supply-chain dynamics remain key monitorable. Cummins remains focused on disciplined execution, price realization, cost management and operational efficiency. The stock is currently trading at a P/E of 35.7x/30.2x for FY28/29E.

We maintain our ‘BUY’ rating on the stock value the stock at a PE of 43x Sep’28E (same earlier) with revised TP of INR 5,334 (INR 5,414 earlier). We are likely to revisit our estimates post the call, factoring in further clarity on demand trends, pricing actions and margin recovery.
